title: Federal Acquisition Regulation: Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul Parts 1, 2, 4, 33, 39, 40, and 53
key_claim: The FAR Council's proposed rule implementing Executive Order 14275 pairs the deletion of non-statutory acquisition requirements with price preferences and incentives for domestically sourced goods and services, and records that roughly 45 percent of FY2025 contract dollars were awarded without competition or with a single offer.
frame_summary: Argues that removing non-statutory requirements and restoring contracting-officer discretion will widen the supplier base while also strengthening domestic-preference outcomes, so simplification and industrial preference are presented as the same reform.
verbatim_quote: The proposed changes also elevate the importance of fiscal responsibility by prioritizing the best use of taxpayer dollars, which includes price preferences and incentives for domestically sourced goods and services.
verbatim_list: OFPP, DoD, GSA, and NASA (collectively referred to as the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council or FAR Council) are proposing to amend the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) to implement Executive Order (E.O.) 14275, Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement.
Interested parties should submit written comments to the Regulatory Secretariat Division at the address shown below on or before July 23, 2026, to be considered in the formation of the final rule.
According to data in the SAM Contract Awards Management, roughly 45 percent of contract dollars were awarded in FY 2025 either without competition or with competition that received only one offer.
notes: Published Document 2026-12559 (91 FR 37550), FAR Case 2026-001, RIN 9000-AO86. title: OMB Releases Four Proposed Rules as Part of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul
key_claim: The four FAR Overhaul proposed rules issued on 23 June 2026 create a sunset process for acquisition rules, consolidate procurement forms, reorganise public notice requirements, and establish a unified cybersecurity framework, with comments due 23 July 2026.
frame_summary: Frames the overhaul as burden relief for small suppliers, which means the new supplier-facing obligations it also creates are presented as simplification rather than as new regulation.
verbatim_list: Specifically, the proposals update the process for protesting a bid and establish a unified cybersecurity framework.
Creating a sunset process, consolidating procurement forms into one website, simplifying definitions, and removing non-essential regulatory requirements.
The release of these four proposed rules is the first installment of a broader overhaul of the FAR, with additional proposed rules expected in subsequent Federal Register notices.
notes: US government source confirming the content and timetable of the four proposed rules.

title: Cloud and AI Development Act
key_claim: The Cloud and AI Development Act defines four cloud and AI sovereignty assurance levels for public sector bodies, with Level 3 requiring providers to be owned and controlled from the EU, and establishes a common EU-level procurement framework so public administrations can use their joint purchasing power.
frame_summary: Argues that Europe can reduce cloud and AI dependency through graded sovereignty requirements and joint public purchasing while keeping the market open to non-EU providers, so procurement is presented as the lever rather than prohibition.
verbatim_quote: The Cloud and AI Development Act defines cloud and AI sovereignty comprising four assurance levels, to be used by public sector bodies based on their risk assessments.
verbatim_list: Level 3: where providers must be owned and controlled from the EU and meet additional criteria, such as personnel citizenship. The Commission can recognise third-country providers;
establishing a common EU-level procurement framework for public administrations to leverage their joint purchasing power;
at least tripling the EU's data centre capacity within the next 5-7 years;

title: The flaws in the European Union's proposed Industrial Accelerator Act and how to fix them
key_claim: The proposed Industrial Accelerator Act introduces Made in EU and low-carbon preferences into public procurement and support schemes, and amends the Net-Zero Industry Act to raise the share of auctioned volume subject to such criteria from 30 percent to 40 percent, or 8 GW per year, whichever is lower.
frame_summary: Argues that origin-based content rules and the 20 percent manufacturing share target are economically unjustified and expose the EU to trade retaliation, and should be replaced by resilience and sustainability criteria plus reciprocity.
verbatim_list: It sets a target for manufacturing to contribute 20 percent of EU GDP by 2035 and introduces 'Made in EU' (or trusted partners) and low-carbon preferences into public procurement and support schemes, along with conditions on foreign direct investment (FDI).

The IAA amends the NZIA to increase the requirement to apply such criteria - now including an explicit 'Made in EU' (Union-origin) requirement - from 30 percent to 40 percent of auctioned volume, or 8 GW per year, whichever is lower.

The proposed IAA target of a 20 percent industry share of GDP by 2035 is identical to one set by the European Commission in a 2012 industrial strategy for 2020 (European Commission, 2012) - a target that was not achieved.
notes: Policy Brief 10/2026, updated 17 June 2026 with clarifications to section 2. Verbatim list normalised for en-dashes and curly quotes; the underlying sentences are as printed.

title: Public Procurement, Trade and Industrial Policies: Supporting National Priorities
key_claim: Public procurement represents about 13% of GDP on average across OECD countries and is increasingly used to pursue priority goals including industrial policy objectives.
frame_summary: Argues that procurement has become the arena where industrial policy and trade policy collide, and that reciprocity of access rather than simple national preference should govern the response.
verbatim_list: Public procurement represents a large share of economic activity in OECD countries (13% of GDP on average) and is increasingly used to pursue priority goals, including industrial policy goals.

title: The draft proposal for the Public Procurement Act has leaked
key_claim: The leak confirmed that the EU procurement reform will take the form of a directly applicable Regulation rather than Directives, which removes national transposition discretion, but at least 17 member states oppose the change and the file may struggle in Council.
frame_summary: Argues that the choice of legal instrument, not the content of the criteria, is the decisive change, because a Regulation unifies the rules that apply day to day and removes the room member states use to bend transposition.
verbatim_quote: I expect the choice of legislative instrument has not gone down well with the member States since we know that at least 17 are dead set against it. So there is a not-insignificant risk that the reform will struggle to pass through the Council.
verbatim_list: My expectation is that the Public Procurement Act will end up having a similar effect on compliance and respect for the (EU) rules similar to the GDPR a decade ago, including enhancing the practical relevance of the Court of Justice judgments.
the move to a Regulation will improve the standing of the discipline and give it the importance consummate with a set of rules influencing 15% of the EU's GDP
notes: Academic specialist analysis by Pedro Telles, professor of public procurement law; classified Tier 2 as expert academic commentary rather than trade press. title: Leaked EU Public Procurement Act (July 2026)
key_claim: The European industry association for indoor climate and cooling technologies told members that the leaked draft would recast EU procurement rules to give buyers wider scope to support European production and supply-chain resilience.
frame_summary: Frames the leaked draft as a commercial risk and opportunity for manufacturers rather than a governance question, which shows how quickly suppliers have started reading procurement law as their binding rulebook.
verbatim_list: An early draft Public Procurement Act would recast EU public procurement rules, giving buyers wider scope to support European production and supply-chain resilience. The proposal remains under development.
notes: Body is members-only; the quoted standfirst is public. Industry association without primary research, so Tier 3.

title: UNI Europa statement on the leaked EU Public Procurement Act
date_evidence: Visible dateline under the headline: '30.07.26'. Year confirmed by the page's own asset path: meta-og:image: https://www.uni-europa.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2026/07/UNI-Europa-statement-on-the-leaked-EU-Public-Procurement-Act-e1785402196928-565x296.jpg
key_claim: The draft leaked on 9 July 2026 would make best price-quality ratio the standard award method with a binding minimum quality weighting of 30 per cent, rising to 50 per cent for labour-intensive contracts, but replacing three Directives with a Regulation risks acting as a ceiling on more ambitious national social criteria.
frame_summary: Argues that the reform's mandatory quality weightings are welcome but that the choice of a directly applicable Regulation removes the national transposition margin that allowed member states to go further on social conditions.
verbatim_quote: Any final instrument must expressly safeguard member states’ ability to maintain or adopt more favourable social provisions.
verbatim_list: There would be a binding minimum quality weighting of 30 per cent, rising to 50 per cent for labour-intensive contracts in UNI Europa sectors such as cleaning and security.
The draft EU Procurement Act leaked on 9 July 2026 overcomes lowest-price tendering, a long-standing demand made by UNI Europa and its social partners in property services.

Second, the choice of a directly applicable Regulation, replacing three EU Directives, risks removing the transposition margin that allowed member states, such as Germany, to build more ambitious collective-agreement-compliance models.
notes: Advocacy source used as directional corroboration on the leaked draft's content and as one side of the counter-argument.
